newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton to head U.S. millennium project.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton to head U.S. millennium project.

text.p: Saying the world is finally "present at the future," President Bill Clinton on Friday announced a White House millennium project designed to usher in the next century with tributes to the past and future.

"The White House millennium program will guide and direct America's celebration of the millennium by showcasing the achievements that define us as a nation -- our culture, our scholarship, our scientific exploration," he said.

First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton will take the "leading role" in overseeing the project, which will include White House lectures, a series of programs sponsored by the National Endowment for the Arts and a preservation program run by the National Archives.

"This gives us a remarkable opportunity to honor the past and to imagine the future and to connect the two in our own minds and for our fellow Americans," Clinton said during a ceremony at the National Archives.
"The 20th century has been called the American century," he said, standing before encased copies of the Constitution, the Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights.

"Through wars and depression and industrial revolution, and now an information revolution, our American spirit of discovery, innovation and faith in the future have carried us forward and inspired billions of people around the world," he said.

"For centuries, people have wondered what this millennium would bring," he said. "Would it signal an apocalypse or herald a new world? ... Whatever the hopes and fears, the millennium is no longer a distant possibility. It has arrived."

"We are present at the future -- a moment we must now define for ourselves and for our children," said Clinton, who used the theme of building a bridge to the 21st century as a key element of his re-election.
The National Endowment for the Arts currently is providing nearly $5.9 million in funds for 29 millennium projects around the country.

The NEA projects include a photographic survey of the United States at the turn of the century and a program by the American Dance Festival in Durham, North Carolina, to commission new jazz and dance works.
Clinton also announced that the United States would accept an invitation by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to particiate in Expo 2000 in Hanover -- the first World's Fair to mark a millennium.
